sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loading settings and paths
sections.what: Loads the local settings files so tests reach the same database, sets the test port (3100 by default), and points at a Chromium browser that a cloud sandbox provides if it exists.
sections.why: The comments say test helpers need the server's database address and the sandbox ships Chromium.
sections.watch_out: The fallback browser path is specific to one image; elsewhere it is ignored and Playwright uses its own browser.

sections.name: default export
sections.title: Test runner settings
sections.what: Sets the test folder, runs tests in parallel, keeps traces for failures, starts the built app on the test port with the design gallery on and a test admin email, and runs only Chrome at desktop size.
sections.why: Likely reason: the design gallery is hidden in production, so tests switch it on.
sections.watch_out: Locally an already-running server is reused, so a stale server with old code can make tests pass or fail wrongly.

summary: Configures the end-to-end browser tests: where they live, which browser they use, and how the app is started for them.
purpose: Run real browser tests against the app's pages.
why: The comments explain that test helpers need the same database as the server, and that the sandbox ships a Chromium browser. Likely reason the gallery is switched on: it is hidden in production.
how: 1) Load the settings files. 2) Set the test folder and the report style. 3) Start the built app on the test port with the test-only switches. 4) Run the tests in Chrome, saving a trace for each failure.
inputs: Settings files and environment variables such as CI, the port number and the browser path.
outputs: Test results, an HTML report in CI, and trace files for failed tests.
risks: The test admin email and the gallery switch exist only for tests; if they leaked into production they would expose extra pages. Retries are zero, so flaky tests fail outright.
debug: If tests cannot reach the app, check the port and that the build exists. If a browser error appears, check the browser path and that the browser is installed. For a failed test, open its trace file.
